claims.text: Scabies is caused by Sarcoptes scabiei var. hominis, the human itch mite
claims.quote: Scabies is caused by the human itch mite (Sarcoptes scabiei var. hominis).

claims.text: The female mite tunnels just beneath the surface of the skin
claims.quote: You may see tiny burrows on the skin, caused by the female mite tunneling just beneath the surface of the skin.

claims.text: An otherwise healthy person may carry fewer than 10 to 15 mites
claims.quote: Fewer than 10 – 15 mites may be present on an infected person who is otherwise healthy.

claims.text: Itch is a hypersensitivity (allergic) reaction to mites and their feces; itching may continue for several weeks after treatment even if all mites and eggs are killed
claims.quote: The itching of scabies is due to a hypersensitivity reaction (allergy) to mites and their feces, so itching may continue for several weeks after treatment even if all the mites and eggs are killed.

claims.text: First infestation: symptoms typically take 4 to 8 weeks to develop
claims.quote: When a person is infested with scabies mites the first time, symptoms typically take 4 – 8 weeks to develop.

claims.text: Adult rash locations: between fingers; wrist, elbow, knee, armpit folds; penis, nipples, waist, buttocks, shoulder blades
claims.quote: between fingers ... in the skin folds of the wrist, elbow, knee, or armpit ... on the penis, nipples, waist, buttocks, and shoulder blades

claims.text: Infants and very young children often have a rash on the head, face, neck, palms, and soles
claims.quote: Infants and very young children often experience a rash on the head, face, neck, palms, and soles of the feet.

claims.text: Most commonly spread by direct, prolonged skin-to-skin contact
claims.quote: Human scabies is most commonly spread by direct, prolonged skin-to-skin contact with a person who has scabies.

claims.text: Mites generally do not survive more than two to three days away from human skin; sharing clothing, towels, bedding is less common
claims.quote: Scabies mites generally do not survive more than two to three days away from human skin. ... Less commonly, sharing clothing, towels, or bedding used by an infected person.

claims.text: Outbreaks more common in nursing homes, extended care facilities, jails and prisons, childcare facilities
claims.quote: Places where scabies outbreaks more commonly occur include: Nursing homes; Extended care facilities; Detention facilities including jails and prisons; Childcare facilities

claims.text: A negative scraping does not rule out scabies
claims.quote: A person can still have scabies even if mites, eggs, or feces are not found.

claims.text: Crusted scabies is very contagious; delayed diagnosis and treatment can often cause outbreaks
claims.quote: Crusted scabies is a severe form of scabies that is very contagious. ... Delayed diagnosis and treatment of crusted scabies can often cause outbreaks.

claims.text: Treat all household members and close contacts at the same time; notify skin-to-skin contacts from the previous two months
claims.quote: To control the spread of scabies, treat all household members and close contacts at the same time as the person with scabies.

claims.text: Notify people with direct skin-to-skin contact during the previous two months
claims.quote: Notify people you had direct skin-to-skin contact with during the previous two months and encourage them to seek treatment.

claims.text: Wash clothing, towels, bedding used next to the skin during the three days before treatment
claims.quote: Wash all clothing, towels, and bedding used next to the skin during the three days before starting treatment.

claims.text: Hot water and hot dryer; above 50 C (122 F) for 10 minutes kills mites and eggs
claims.quote: Wash bedding, clothing, and towels in hot water and dry in a hot dryer. ... temperatures in excess of 50°C or 122°F for 10 minutes will kill mites and eggs.

claims.text: Dry-clean or seal in a closed plastic bag for at least 72 hours to a week
claims.quote: Dry-clean items that can't be washed or seal them in a closed plastic bag for at least 72 hours to a week.

claims.text: No over-the-counter products are approved to treat scabies
claims.quote: No over-the-counter, non-prescription products are approved to treat human scabies.

claims.text: CDC lists permethrin 5% cream and oral ivermectin as first-line medications for classic scabies
claims.quote: First line medications: Permethrin cream 5% ... Ivermectin oral tablet

claims.text: Permethrin and ivermectin have similar efficacy for cure
claims.quote: However, topical permethrin and oral ivermectin have similar efficacy for cure of scabies.

claims.text: Permethrin is FDA approved for scabies in people at least 2 months of age
claims.quote: Permethrin is approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for the treatment of scabies ... in people who are at least 2 months of age.

claims.text: Permethrin applied from the neck down and washed off after 8 to 14 hours
claims.quote: Permethrin 5% cream applied to all areas of the body from the neck down and washed off after 8–14 hours.

claims.text: A second application about a week later may be needed
claims.quote: However, two (or more) applications, each about a week apart, may be necessary to eliminate all mites.

claims.text: Oral ivermectin is not FDA approved for scabies
claims.quote: Oral ivermectin is not FDA approved for the treatment of scabies.

claims.text: Ivermectin two doses of 200 mcg/kg with food, 7 to 14 days apart
claims.quote: two doses of oral ivermectin (200µg/kg/dose) should be taken with food ... each 7 to 14 days apart.

claims.text: Scabies experts recommend taking ivermectin with a meal to increase bioavailability
claims.quote: scabies experts recommend taking with a meal to increase bioavailability.

claims.text: Safety of ivermectin not established in children under 15 kg or in pregnant women
claims.quote: The safety of ivermectin in children weighing less than 15 kg and in pregnant women has not been established.

claims.text: Same 200 mcg/kg per dose used for scabies (paired with label weight table)
claims.quote: two doses of oral ivermectin (200µg/kg/dose) should be taken with food

claims.text: Crusted scabies: ivermectin given together with a topical agent; permethrin to entire body with an oral agent
claims.quote: For crusted scabies, ivermectin should be administered together with a topical agent. ... For crusted scabies, topical permethrin should be applied to the entire body and administered together with an oral agent.

claims.text: Crusted ivermectin 200 mcg/kg; no consensus; 3, 5 or 7 doses on listed days depending on severity
claims.quote: Some experts recommend administering oral ivermectin (200µg/kg/dose) in three doses (approximately days 1, 2, and 8) ... five doses (approximately days 1, 2, 8, 9, and 15) ... seven doses (approximately days 1, 2, 8, 9, 15, 22, and 29)

claims.text: Dose number depends on infection severity; no consensus on frequency
claims.quote: There is no consensus on the optimal frequency of ivermectin administration. ... depending on infection severity

claims.text: Permethrin frequency in crusted scabies: daily to every 2 to 3 days for the first 1 to 2 weeks
claims.quote: experts have recommended anywhere from an initial daily application to application every 2-3 days for the first 1-2 weeks.

claims.text: Keratolytic cream on crusted areas on non-permethrin days until crusting resolves
claims.quote: A topical keratolytic cream may also be used to help reduce the crusting of the skin ... The cream may be applied to areas of crusting on days that permethrin is not given, until crusting has resolved.

claims.quote: everyone who has had close contact with that person need treatment. ... Recent sexual partners

claims.text: An antibiotic is used to clear an infection
claims.quote: Antibiotic: To wipe out an infection.

claims.quote: Temperatures in excess of 50°C or 122°F for 10 minutes will kill mites and eggs.

claims.quote: Staff generally can return to work the day after receiving a dose of treatment with permethrin or ivermectin ... Use gloves when giving hands-on care to any patient/resident with suspect or confirmed scabies

claims.text: Identify and treat all exposed persons; offer treatment to household members of staff
claims.quote: Identify and treat all persons (e.g., staff, relatives, patients/residents) ... Offer treatment to household members (e.g., spouses, children, roommates) of staff

claims.text: Keep records (name, age, sex, room number) and run an early detection program
claims.quote: Have an active program for early detection of infested patients/residents and staff. ... Maintain records with patient/resident name, age, sex, room number.

claims.text: Hot wash and dry; plastic bag several days to a week; routine cleaning and vacuuming; environmental disinfestation not necessary

claims.text: Store non-launderable items in closed plastic bag several days to a week; routine cleaning and vacuuming
claims.quote: Items that cannot be laundered can be disinfested by storing in a closed plastic bag for several days to a week. ... Routine cleaning and vacuuming of the room should be done

claims.text: Adult female mites measure about 0.3 to 0.5 mm
claims.quote: The males of this species measure 210–290 μm, while the females measure 300–500 μm in length.

claims.text: Transmission of animal mites to humans is rare
claims.quote: from animals to humans is rare, with the most common transmission occurring from dogs.

claims.text: Burrows contain adult female mites, their eggs, and excreta
claims.quote: The presence of burrows containing adult female mites, their eggs, and excreta is the diagnostic hallmark of scabies.

claims.text: Burrows pathognomonic; whitish, grayish or brownish, about 10 mm long, pearl-like vesicle
claims.quote: The presence of the female mite's burrow is pathognomonic ... Typically, burrows are whitish, grayish, or brownish in color and measure about 0.5 mm wide and 10 mm long.

claims.text: Pruritic papules on glans penis almost always pathognomonic
claims.quote: The presence of pruritic papules, particularly on the glans penis in adult males, is almost always pathognomonic for scabies.

claims.text: Face and scalp involvement in infants, elderly, immunodeficient
claims.quote: However, infants, the elderly, those with crusted scabies, and individuals with immunodeficiency may experience involvement of the face and scalp.

claims.text: Brief contact such as handshake rare, requires 15 to 20 minutes; sexual contact significant route
claims.quote: Transmission through brief contact, such as handshakes and medical examinations, is rare since it usually requires 15–20 minutes. ... Sexual contact is also a significant route of transmission

claims.text: Microscopy of skin scraping with blunt blade and mineral oil; negative does not exclude
claims.quote: gently scraping the skin with a blunt‐edged scalpel blade (size 10 or 15) while placing 1–2 drops of mineral oil ... whereas a negative result does not exclude it.

claims.text: Definitive diagnosis by microscopic examination of skin scrapings
claims.quote: Definitive diagnosis typically involves direct microscopic examination of skin scrapings obtained from these burrows

claims.text: Dermoscopy delta sign and jet trail
claims.quote: the brown‐black triangle, which represents the mite itself (known as the delta sign), followed by a white smoke sign, which represents the burrow (known as the jet trail)

claims.text: Clinical diagnosis from contact history, itch after contact, typical distribution
claims.quote: Scabies can be diagnosed if the patient has a history of contact with a scabies‐infested individual, itching that commenced subsequent to the contact, and exhibits typical distribution and lesions.

claims.text: Apparent permethrin resistance may reflect application errors
claims.quote: some studies suggest that this resistance may not be accurate and that the ineffectiveness may be due to application errors.

claims.text: Scabies medicines less effective against eggs; repeat a week later
claims.quote: Scabies medications are generally less effective against the eggs. Therefore, treatment should be repeated a week later to kill newly hatched mites.

claims.text: Permethrin generally preferred in pregnancy and breastfeeding given limited ivermectin data
claims.quote: However, due to limited data on the use of ivermectin in pregnant and breastfeeding women, treatment with permethrin should be preferred.

claims.text: Ivermectin for scabies not associated with serious adverse events to date
claims.quote: To date, the use of ivermectin for the treatment of scabies has not been associated with any serious adverse events.

claims.text: Crusted scabies: thousands or even millions of mites
claims.quote: caused by an unlimited multiplication of mites in the skin, resulting in thousands or even millions of specimens.

claims.text: Host factors more important; more than half have immunosuppressive risk factors; HIV 45% in one case series
claims.quote: More than half of crusted scabies patients have identifiable immunosuppressive risk factors ... In a case series of crusted scabies, HIV infection was reported as the most common comorbidity in 45% of patients.

claims.text: Host factors play a larger role than mite characteristics
claims.quote: Host factors play a more significant role in crusted scabies than pathogen‐specific characteristics such as the parasite's virulence.

claims.text: Risk: elderly; amputations, paralysis, Alzheimer disease, finger deformities, nutritional disorders, Down syndrome
claims.quote: Patients with amputations, paralysis, Alzheimer's disease, finger deformities, nutritional disorders, Down syndrome, or those with weak cognitive abilities or physical impairments, may not feel itching

claims.text: Crusted scabies in elderly (reduced immune response)
claims.quote: The clinical presentation of scabies may also differ in elderly individuals due to their decreased immune response. Crusted scabies may develop in elderly patients.

claims.text: Crust can exceed 1 cm, resembles psoriasis, creamy/gray/yellow-brown
claims.quote: These plaques have a parakeratotic crust that can exceed 1 cm in thickness and closely resemble psoriasis or Darier's disease. ... creamy, gray, yellow‐brown, or yellow‐green variations

claims.text: Nails thickened, discolored, significant source of relapse
claims.quote: Nails are a significant source of relapses and have a discolored, thickened, and dystrophic appearance.

claims.text: About half of crusted scabies patients have some itch
claims.quote: Although it is commonly believed that pruritus is absent in crusted scabies, half of all patients with this condition experience some degree of pruritus

claims.text: Crusted scabies transmitted via bed covers and sofas and shed scales; majority of outbreaks
claims.quote: frequently transmitted through objects like bed covers and sofas. Accordingly, patients with crusted scabies are involved in the majority of outbreaks. ... transmission can also occur through shed scales from these patients.

claims.text: Contacts treated at the same time even without symptoms; absence of itch does not mean absence of disease
claims.quote: All individuals in close contact with the infected person, such as family members, children's school friends, and sexual partners, should be treated at the same time, even if they do not have symptoms.

claims.text: Absence of itching in a family member does not signify absence of disease
claims.quote: It is crucial to recognize that the absence of itching in a family member does not necessarily signify the absence of the disease.

claims.text: Sealed plastic bags for items such as children's fabrics and stuffed animals
claims.quote: storing items, such as clothing, linens, bedding, children's fabrics, and stuffed animals in sealed plastic bags, may reduce the spread of scabies.

claims.text: Nodules persist weeks to months after treatment and typically lack mites
claims.quote: Notably, these nodules do not necessarily indicate an active infestation and typically do not contain mites. Nodular scabies can persist for weeks or even months after effective scabies treatment.

claims.text: Permethrin irritant contact dermatitis leads to discontinuation in about 5%
claims.quote: Permethrin may cause irritant contact dermatitis in some individuals, which can lead to discontinuation of treatment in approximately 5% of patients.

claims.text: One case of crusted scabies is considered an outbreak
claims.quote: Only one case of crusted scabies is considered an outbreak.

claims.text: Secondary bacterial infections such as impetigo and furuncles
claims.quote: A clinically distinct polymorphism occurs with the intermingling of excoriations and erythematous papules, occasional secondary eczematizations, pustular lesions, and pyodermic lesions such as impetigo and furuncles.

claims.text: Scabies carries stigma
claims.quote: Scabies can also have significant psychosocial and economic impacts due to stigmatization and loss of workforce.

claims.text: Comparison table: permethrin preferred in pregnancy (with refs 2, 9, 10)
claims.quote: due to limited data on the use of ivermectin in pregnant and breastfeeding women, treatment with permethrin should be preferred.

claims.text: Longer than the 4 to 6 weeks in earlier published guidance

claims.text: Older combined-treatment group had more itch, 42% vs 25%, not significant

claims.text: Post-scabies itch led to additional health care utilization

claims.text: 83% treated with topical corticosteroids; about half gentle skin care; gabapentin, doxepin, NB-UVB in few

claims.text: Reinfestation by untreated family members or partner explained some failures
